title: Showing a notification
summary: Turns a content-free push into a readable notification on the phone. iOS: a notification service extension. Android: the push handler. Both fetch and decrypt the event on the device with the SDK notification client, then show sender, chat and text.

roomId.description: The chat. Notifications group by it.

title.description: DM: the sender's name. Group: the group name.

body.description: The plain text, the media kind, or a fixed line (see notes).

senderName.description: Group only: shown before the body.

isInvite.description: true for an invite to a chat or group.

result.description: shown: decrypted. fallback: the event could not be fetched or decrypted in time; a generic line shows. dropped: nothing to show (own event, read on another device, a muted chat).

receive.effect: Opens the shared SDK store, gets a NotificationClient and calls getNotification for the room and event within the platform's time limit, then shows, falls back or drops.

open.effect: A tap on the notification opens chat-timeline for the room, scrolled to the event.

markRead.effect: When the chat is read on any device, removes its notifications (on the next push or app start).

notes: iOS: the extension runs with little memory and about 30 s. It uses NotificationProcessSetup for several processes and the same session store in the app group. Never start a full sync there.
fallback shows bipe_app_notification_fallback (a new message, no sender text) so a push is never lost and never shows ciphertext.
A message from someone who is not a contact and has no chat yet is a chat request (parity requests): title from the sender, body bipe_app_notification_dm_request, no message text.
Media and others: image, video, voice, file and sticker use their fixed lines; a reaction uses bipe_app_notification_reaction with the emoji; edits and deletions show nothing new.
No scam check runs on the notification text in phase 1; the warning shows in the chat (message-scam-warning).
Calls are out of scope (plan section 4, phase 3).
